title: Verdigris
protagonist: Dr. Ezra Mokwena, mycologist — and the mycelium that is arguably the book's second narrator
logline: As the warming Earth turns fungal and the spores learn to ride human beings like puppets, the last weapon that works is copper — a colloidal mist that scours the growth clean. But the mycologist holding the sprayer comes to believe the bloom is not an invader: it is the planet's immune response to a species that stopped being human, and the mushrooms rising in every ruin are trying to give that humanity back before the copper kills the only thing that could.
blueprint: Original sci-fi horror / eco-weird. Runaway warming past the wet-bulb threshold collapses the barrier between fungal and human biology; a heat-adapted Cordyceps-Aspergillus complex spreads aflatoxin-bearing spores that neurologically hijack ('zombify') hosts. Humanity's one reliable counter is copper — colloidal copper mist, oligodynamic, denatures the growth. Against this: a mycologist reading the psychedelic fungi (psilocybin, and a widening pharmacopeia of other entheogenic plants) as a message rather than a menace, and the terrible question of whether the cure and the disease are the same organism. No borrowed IP.
market: literary sci-fi horror / eco-weird / climate-gothic — original IP, for the shelf
lineage: original — no borrowed IP. Kinship of engine only (declared, never transcribed): the fungal-apocalypse tradition, the ambiguous-invader ecohorror, the entheogen-as-message strand. All world, cast, scenes and beats original.
